title: Scientists Trained an AI Video Model Using LIVING Brain Cells!
summary: San Francisco startup The Biological Computing Co. launched mischief 1, the first publicly available image-to-video model optimized using laboratory recordings of living biological neurons. Running as a lightweight software adapter over Wan 2.2 on standard GPUs, the company claims it delivers matching visual quality 5x faster and at an 80% lower compute cost.
raw_text: So check this out, because we have officially entered sci-fi territory. A startup in San Francisco called The Biological Computing Co. just dropped a new image-to-video model called mischief 1. And here's the wild part: they didn't just train it on regular computer chips. They actually grew between 100,000 and 500,000 living neurons on high-density electrode arrays in a lab, stimulated them with electrical signals from videos, and recorded how those living brain cells fired! Then, they translated those biological visual tracking rules into a tiny digital software adapter that sits on top of the open-weight Wan 2.2 video model. Honestly, this is huge if their numbers hold up. Because it runs on normal digital GPUs, we don't need wetware at home, and they claim it runs at least five times faster and slashes compute costs by 80 percent! You can generate a five-second 720p clip for just five cents. Now, I have to be real with you guys—independent reviewers are pointing out that these benchmarks are self-reported right now, so we need to test this ourselves. Still, using real living brain cells to make AI way cheaper is completely mind-blowing!

Plus, it's up to 69 percent faster than their old agent. If you have Canva Pro, I definitely think this is going to save us hours of tedious layout tweaking.

title: Forget Prompting! This New AI Reads Your Brainwaves to Generate Art
summary: Wearable brain-computer interface startup Sabi introduced Reinforcement Learning with Neural Feedback (RLNF), a post-training technique that steers generative AI models using passive EEG brain signals and eye tracking. Tested on the FLUX.2 Klein 4B image model, the system customized facial generation to match individual user aesthetics without manual clicks or labels.
raw_text: So check this out—what if you didn't even have to click thumbs-up or type a massive prompt to get an AI to learn your exact taste? A brain-computer interface startup called Sabi just introduced something they call Reinforcement Learning with Neural Feedback, or RLNF. Instead of making humans click preference buttons to train an AI, they strapped EEG brain monitors and eye trackers onto five test participants while they passively looked at 420 different anchor faces. Here's the wild part: Sabi's system decoded their unconscious brain signals—specifically posterior alpha suppression between 8 and 13 Hertz—to figure out which facial traits sparked an arousal or aesthetic reward response in their brains. Then, they fed those brain scores straight into a LoRA adapter on top of the FLUX.2 Klein 4B image generator! Without the users ever typing a word or clicking a single rating, the AI automatically shifted its image generation toward the exact facial structures each individual person subconsciously liked. Honestly, this is equal parts fascinating and a little creepy. We don't have pricing on Sabi's wearable hardware yet, but brain-steered AI is officially a real thing!

title: Why Coding Agents Are Broken—And How Factory Droid 1.0 & Vercel Just Fixed Them!
summary: Developer tooling firm Factory launched Factory Droid 1.0, a model-independent coding agent harness that uses sandboxed JavaScript Script Mode to achieve a 65.2% pass rate on Terminal-Bench 4 while outperforming Cursor and Devin. Meanwhile, Vercel Labs open-sourced agent-desktop v1.0.2, replacing heavy screenshot vision parsing with OS accessibility-tree traversal to cut token usage by up to 96%.
raw_text: If you build with coding agents or computer-use AI, we need to talk about how much money we are wasting on context bloat. Right now, standard agents pass every single tool output and screenshot back into the LLM, burning millions of tokens. Well, two massive releases just fixed this. First, Factory launched Droid 1.0, and instead of doing slow back-and-forth chat tool calls, it uses 'Script Mode'. The AI writes a sandboxed JavaScript program that fires off hundreds of concurrent tool calls and only sends the final printed summary back to the model. In one test, resolving 151 Linear issues took just 61,000 tokens instead of 3.1 million, beating both Cursor and Devin on Terminal-Bench 4! Second, check out what Vercel Labs just open-sourced: agent-desktop v1.0.2. Instead of taking screenshots and using slow vision models that hijack your mouse pointer, it reads the native OS accessibility tree in the background using a 3-level skeleton mode. That cuts token consumption on dense apps like Slack and VS Code by up to 96 percent. For developers, these two harnesses are absolute game-changers.

title: ISRO's Midnight Rocket Launch Just Saved India's Sovereign GPS System!
summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launched the GSLV-F18 rocket carrying the 2,232-kg NVS-03 navigation satellite from Sriharikota into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit. The mission restores India's regional NavIC satellite constellation to the minimum four-satellite configuration required for standalone positioning services.
raw_text: So check this out—just before midnight on October 30th, ISRO lit up the night sky in Sriharikota with the launch of the GSLV-F18 rocket, and this wasn't just another routine space mission. They were carrying the 2,232-kilogram NVS-03 satellite, and honestly, India's entire independent navigation network was riding on this launch. Earlier this year, Parliament revealed that aging satellites and atomic clock failures had knocked India's sovereign GPS alternative—called NavIC—down to just three working satellites. And here is the catch: you mathematically need at least four active satellites in orbit to provide standalone positioning! Without a fourth satellite, NavIC could only keep time, not track locations. Using an indigenous cryogenic upper stage, GSLV-F18 nailed the orbital injection with incredible precision, coming within just 50 meters of its target perigee of 170.36 kilometers! Now that NVS-03 is up there, NavIC is officially back to full four-satellite strength, covering India and 1,500 kilometers beyond its borders, plus adding civilian L1 frequency support so everyday phones and trackers can lock right in.

title: Why AI Giants Are Spending Millions on 1950s Magnetic Tape Technology!
summary: Fujifilm announced a 10 billion yen ($64 million) capital investment at its Kanagawa Factory to increase magnetic data-storage tape production capacity fivefold by fiscal year 2028. Marks Fujifilm's first tape expansion in 20 years, the ramp focuses on LTO Ultrium 10 cartridges holding up to 100 TB compressed to serve surging AI cold-archiving demand.
raw_text: Here's a tech plot twist I bet you didn't see coming: the hottest storage hardware for the 2026 AI boom is literally magnetic tape! That's right—Fujifilm just announced they are pouring 64 million dollars into their factory in Japan to quintuple their magnetic tape production over the next two years. This is the first time in 20 years they've expanded tape capacity! Why are massive AI data centers buying tape like crazy? Because training frontier AI models generates petabytes of raw data that companies legally and operationally have to save forever, and keeping all that cold data spinning on hard drives or SSDs is way too expensive. Check out the specs on modern tape: a single Fujifilm LTO Ultrium 10 cartridge uses hybrid barium and strontium ferrite particles to pack 40 terabytes of native data—or up to 100 terabytes compressed—into the palm of your hand, transferring at 400 megabytes per second! Plus, once you unplug a tape cartridge and put it on a shelf, it is physically air-gapped, meaning ransomware hackers can never touch it. And by LTO-14, they are targeting 365 terabytes per cartridge!

title: North Korean Hackers Just Stole $6.3 BILLION From Binance in the Biggest Crypto Heist Ever!
summary: North Korean state-backed hacking group TraderTraitor stole a record $6.3 billion in digital assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance—more than four times larger than any previous crypto heist. The attackers compromised a DevOps engineer's laptop and exploited Ethereum's EIP-7702 smart contract standard to drain Binance's main Ethereum wallet, though stablecoin issuers froze nearly 40% of the funds and Binance covered all user losses.
raw_text: Honestly, this is the wildest cybersecurity story of the decade. North Korean hackers just pulled off the biggest cryptocurrency heist in human history, stealing an unbelievable 6.3 BILLION dollars from Binance! That is more than four times bigger than the previous record holder. Here's the wild part about how the TraderTraitor hacking group pulled it off: they didn't just brute-force a password. They hacked a Binance DevOps engineer's laptop, quietly rehearsed the heist for 36 hours across test wallets, and then exploited a newer Ethereum feature called EIP-7702. That standard lets a smart contract temporarily take over a wallet if it gets an authorized encrypted message—which they hijacked to bypass Binance's security approvals and drain the main Ethereum wallet completely dry! Then, their malware literally self-destructed to wipe all the forensic logs! Now, before you panic if you hold crypto on Binance, about 40 percent of the stolen haul was in stablecoins, so Circle, Tether, and Ripple immediately froze those wallets, and Binance put up over 6.34 billion dollars of its own reserves to cover every single dime of user losses.
